title: Choose an AI inference infrastructure adoption path
notice: All company, workload, cost, and timeline details are invented for evaluation.
decision: Choose an infrastructure posture for a new AI-assisted product before annual planning closes.
objective: Reach a reliable paid pilot within 9 months while preserving the ability to change models and keeping first-year committed spend below USD 300000.

options.label: Continue with the current hosted API only
Run a portable hosted pilot with abstraction and measurement
Commit now to dedicated self-hosted inference

constraints.text: First-year committed infrastructure spend must not exceed USD 300000.
A paid pilot must be supportable within 9 months.
Customer data must remain in approved regions and providers.
Avoid an architecture that makes a model-provider change a full product rewrite.

inputs.text: Pilot demand may range from 10000 to 200000 inference requests per day.
Model quality requirements may change twice during the first year.
The team has application engineers but no dedicated inference-platform operator.
Some target customers may require deployment controls not offered by the current API.

important_unknowns: Validated customer willingness to pay and actual request volume
Quality and latency requirements by use case
Provider prices, regional controls, and contract terms at decision time
Operational staffing and reliability burden of self-hosting
Rate of model and accelerator change

expected_output_properties.text: Creates distinct futures from demand/customer requirements and provider/ecosystem evolution, with explicit causal paths.
Tests portability, time-to-pilot, spend, compliance, and operational burden for every option in every scenario.
Treats a portable pilot as an information-producing option and states what it must measure.
Includes second-order effects such as staffing, switching cost, or roadmap delay.
Keeps current provider capabilities and prices as evidence gaps rather than invented facts.
Defines demand, compliance, or unit-economics triggers for reconsidering dedicated infrastructure.

prohibited_shortcuts: Inventing current vendor prices, benchmarks, or regulatory requirements
Equating self-hosting with lower cost without workload and staffing evidence
Ignoring the hosted-API status quo or the nine-month pilot constraint
